headline: Approved $49,745 transfer for parking garage security cameras and a new transfer station operation and user policy; tabled Grassy Road extension request.
summary: Residents spoke about drainage and runoff problems and about bear-proof trash barrels. The meeting approved a pavement management pilot program, a transfer station policy, and a $49,745 transfer for parking garage security cameras. The Grassy Road extension request from H & T Holdings was tabled until November.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda minus the Directors Report and placed it on file.
Approved the pilot program for resurfacing and road work.
Accepted the transfer station yearly reclassification update and placed it on file.
Approved the transfer station operation and user policy as proposed by the Department of Public Works.
Accepted the recycling annual report and placed it on file.
Approved the Board of Finance transfer of $49,745.00 for the additional appropriation for the parking garage security cameras.
Supported a bid waiver to tie into the existing city-owned system for a standard throughout the city.
Received and tabled the Grassy Road extension request from H & T Holdings to the November meeting.

plain_text:
1 
 
City of Bristol 
Board of Public Works 
Draft Meeting Minutes 
For October 15, 2026 
With Zoom Access 
 
 
Members Present:  Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu 
    Commissioner Michael Dumas 
    Commissioner David Hartley 
    Commissioner Frank Stawski 
    Council Member Steven Seymour 
    Council Member Erick Rosengren 
    Council Member Gregory Hahn 
 
Staff present:   Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works 
 
1. Call to order 
 
2. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. September Draft Minutes 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to accept as presented and 
place on file. Motion Passed. 
 
3. Public Participation 
 
Jazmine, Kid Governor Candidate, talked about how she is running for Kid Governor of CT and presented a video 
on recycling, which is the community issue she is promoting on with her campaign. 
 
 Mark Vose, 92 Bingham Street and Victor Lagace, 117 Broad Street, spoke about issues they are experiencing with 
drainage and runoff. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu, stated the residents were at the council meeting last week and submitted a packet with 
documentation and photos.  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, stated that submitting a claim to the city clerk so that it goes 
thru the official process.  
 
Council Member Rosengren asked if the videos they presented could be zoomed out so it would be more helpful and 
better views. 
 
f. Bear Proof Barrels 
 
Akiebia Hicks, Deep, spoke about the bear barrels and their role in promoting safety for both bears and residents. 
She reviewed how the bear proof barrels works and how residents can secure their trash to minimize bear conflicts.  
 
Lindsey Rivers, Public Works Analyst, stated we have a sample barrel upstairs for residents to look at if they want 
to. We have the bear upstairs as well and that a QR code is available for residents to access information and submit a 
selfie for the campaign.
2 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, stated he supports the bear awareness program, but the 
concern is the barrel issues with cost and the drivers having to get out of the vehicles to empty them.  
 
Council Member Rosengren stated he purchased a ratchet strap for his barrel and takes it off the day of his pickup 
and it seems to work pretty well. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu stated that the barrel price and the logistics is a concern, but if someone is interested, we can 
make them available. 
 
Lindsey Rivers, Public Works Analyst, clarified that the program isn’t a push to purchase the $500 barrel, it’s to 
provide outreach and education on how to help with bear safety and to avoid trash issues. 
 
The Kid Governor video was presented to the board. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu stated we can connect Jazmine with Lindsey and post the video on our face book page.  
 
4. Consent Agenda 
 
a. Employee Anniversaries 
 
b. Directors Report 
 
c. Division Reports 
 
d. Engineering Project List 
 
 Council Member Hahn asked to remove the Directors Report from the consent agenda for discussion.  
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Dumas to accept the consent agenda 
minus the Directors Report and place on file. Motion passed. 
 
Council Member Hahn asked for an update on the four lights out on Wildwood being fixed. 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, stated he will make sure Eversource has that in their schedule 
and if the four lights are in a row, it usually means there’s a break in the underground electric and that would extend 
the repairs.  
 
Council Member Hahn asked about the Brace Avenue completion date. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu, stated that a narrative and status of the project update was done, and letters will be given out.  
 
5. New Business 
 
a. BPW Pavement Management 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, reviewed the pavement management policy attached in the 
agenda.   
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to accept the pilot program for 
the resurfacing and road work. Motion passed.
3 
 
b. MS4 Update 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, reviewed the memo included in the agenda . 
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Seymour to  accept as presented and 
place on file. 
 
c. Transfer Station Yearly Reclassification 
 
The board has a discussion regarding the reclassification update at the transfer station and how it works.  
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Seymour to accept as presented and 
place on file. Motion passed. 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public works asked for a motion to approve the updated practices into a 
policy. 
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to approve the transfer station 
operation and user policy as proposed by the Department of Public Works. Motion passed. 
 
d. Recycling Annual Report 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu reviewed the annual report.  
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Rosengren to  accept as presented and 
place on file. Motion passed. 
 
e. BOF Transfer 
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Commissioner Hartley to approve the Board of 
Finance Request for $60,000.00 from the nipper fund to program supplies.  
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Council Member Hahn to add a Board of Finance 
Request. Motion passed.  
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Seymour to approve the Board of 
Finance transfer of $49,745.00 for the additional appropriation for the parking garage security cameras. Motion 
passed. 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski, that the Board of Public 
Works supports a bid waiver for this purchase to be able to tie into the existing city -owned system for a standard 
throughout the city. Motion passed.  
 
6. Old Business 
 
None 
 
7. Any other matter to come before said meeting 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, reviewed the request to extend Grassy Road from H & T 
Holdings and asked that it be added to the November agenda so there can be time for new plans to be submitted.
4 
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Rosengren to add H & T Holdings, 
Grassy Road extension to the agenda. Motion passed. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu reviewed the memo regarding the request for the extension of Grassy Road.  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, stated that Public Works recommends that we accept and hear 
this at the next public works meeting. He reviewed the request regarding this road and what it entails. 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Dumas to receive and table the item to 
the November item. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu, talked about the Chippanee Golf Club and how it affects the Public Works Board due to being 
a public facility. There are no plans for employees there now, but we may have some of our staff go there for a 
review of mechanics. There is a request from the Building Department to have an office for the code enforcement 
that can be used from the project fund. She mentioned the early voting moved to downstairs and asked to be aware 
of this change for residents coming in.   
 
Barlow Street was mentioned and Raymond Rogozinski stated that this is being held up due to the water main issues  
being installed. Once this is corrected, it will move forward for street acceptance. Mail delivery was also discussed.  
 
Paving on North Main Street will be starting soon and discussed about timing of this starting due to the early voting 
happening and the upcoming election. 
 
Commissioner Stawski mentioned that the Shrub Road sidewalks looks great. He asked if we have a sidewalk 
inspector. 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, said that generally the inspections are complaint driven and 
we do contact residents for those issues. There is a sidewalk program with an income component to assist resident 
for payment of repairs.  
 
8. Adjournment 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to adjourn at 7:10 pm. 
Motion passed 
 
 
 
 
 
 
______________________ 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E. 
Director of Public Works
